instructions: Tools over the War of the Realms rule index at /home/oridon/wotr-rule-index. Claude Code sessions in the repo skip the natalie call: CLAUDE.md already imports NATALIE.md. Every other client calls natalie once at the start of a session (it is on the ops surface; a client without it reads NATALIE.md from its project knowledge). Rule loading is lean: once a session, before the first writing, load_rules(tags=[], brief=True), every live rule as one line; load a domain in full (load_rules with its applies_to tags: prose-law for any prose; combat, adjudication, magic-mechanism, pov, dialogue, register, naming, items, scene-structure, mass-combat, stats, magic-design, codex, worldbuilding, standing-inventory, character-sheet, documents, verification, session-protocol) the first time the work touches it, and do not re-read after compaction. Rules print newest pack first; the newer governs where two overlap. The WOTR skills are on this server: skill() lists them, skill(name) loads one to follow; start with wotr-start.

tools.name: load_rules
tools.description:
Load the rules in force for a task. tags: applies_to tags (see instructions).
status defaults to ["live"]. brief=True returns one line per rule, id: summary.
tags=[] with brief=True is the whole live rulebook: read it once a session.
part=N (from 1) returns it in batches of ~25k tokens for clients that truncate
long results; the header names the part count. Read every part.

tools.name: rule
tools.description: One rule in full by id, e.g. R12-3-COMBAT_EXCHANGE_OWES or R13-C.

tools.name: natalie
tools.description:
desktop/NATALIE.md, Natalie's standing instructions: who Natalie is, the
table rules, the culture inventories. Read it at the start of
any WOTR session. section = a heading's words to return just that part.
With no section, desktop/NATALIE.gpt.md (the ChatGPT overlay) is appended at the end
under a header that Claude skips; section = "ChatGPT" returns the overlay alone.

tools.name: natalie_gpt
tools.description:
desktop/NATALIE.gpt.md, the overlay for ChatGPT sessions only. Call it right after
natalie when you are a GPT model: how to read NATALIE.md (act instead of asking,
which rule wins, where numbers come from), your own prose tells, and a worked example
of the prose Isaac wants. Claude sessions do not need it.

tools.name: check_docket
tools.description:
Pending open rulings and proposed (never-ratified) rules touching these tags.
If one would materially change what you are about to write, ask Isaac before writing.

tools.name: list_conflicts
tools.description: CONFLICTS.md: live rules that contradict each other, awaiting Isaac's ruling.

tools.name: archive_scene
tools.description:
Save a finished scene. Writes scenes/<slug>.md (title as the H1, author notes
appended under '## Author notes'), copies it to the wiki's Scene Archive as a private
page, commits and pushes. Returns the file paths.

tools.name: wiki_write
tools.description:
Write a whole wiki page (the Obsidian vault; Notion is retired) and push it:
the Ledger, a Front, any page. path is relative to wiki/, e.g.
'The Table — Running Pieces/The Ledger.md'. markdown is
the full page, frontmatter included if it has one; an existing page's frontmatter
is kept when markdown brings none. The public site rebuilds on push; pages in
private folders or with 'private: true' stay off it.

tools.name: log_ruling
tools.description:
Record a ruling Isaac made at the table (rule_id may be a rule id, a CONFLICTS id
like C-001, or 'new'). Appended to RULINGS.md and pushed; applied to the index
in the next Claude Code session.

tools.name: sync_now
tools.description:
Run build/sync.sh: commit and push wiki edits made in Obsidian (the site rebuilds) and render the Ledger, Fronts and roster pages.
Takes a minute or two.

tools.name: wiki
tools.description:
Search the wiki (the Obsidian vault, the source since 2026-10-15) by meaning and by keyword. Returns the best
matches with the passages that matched, and the full text of the top page (capped)
when full=True. limit is how many
pages come back; raise it when surveying what exists rather than looking one up.

tools.name: character
tools.description:
A character's card from the wiki mirror (the Volume I-V Character Cards and
single-character sections), full text. Say if none exists rather than inventing.

tools.name: fow_line
tools.description:
The Fracture of Worlds line for a named practitioner, pulled from their card:
Level / Stage / Band, the stat table, force-and-flow figures, EU reserve, eta.
If the card has no numbers, says so. Never invent a number.

tools.name: scene_recall
tools.description:
Search the scene archive (scenes/) for continuity: who said what, what happened
where. Matches by meaning as well as by keyword, so describe the moment in your
own words. Returns the best-matching scenes with the passages that matched.
limit is how many scenes come back; raise it when tracing how a thread connects
across the archive rather than looking up one moment.
old_lore=True searches the archive from before the 2026-10-18 lore reset
(lore/v1/scenes) instead; every hit is labelled old lore and is never canon for
events in the current lore, only a record of what was written then.

tools.name: session_start
tools.description:
Where a thread stands, in one call, for any thread name (R79-8): the thread's last
archived scene (title, date and its last ~1,500 words), the Standing Inventory for the
culture, the Ledger lines that have come due, and the inbox count. For Natalie's eyes
only; nothing from it is printed as a recap. scene_type is kept for callers and unused:
load_rules and fow_line are called when the scene needs them.

tools.name: verify_scene
tools.description:
Mechanical prose checks on a draft before it is posted (R79-3 to R79-7): em dashes,
antithesis, countdown negation, the Ladder, apparatus-as-subject, hypophora,
exact stock phrases (R81-9: single words and canon signatures are free), stale
devices. No rhythm, length or count checks: the word count prints as
information (no word count, Isaac 2026-10-30). Jargon, glosses, modern words
and emotion said aloud are free (R80-22, R80-24, R80-26).
combat=True adds blade body/action and anatomy evidence (plain parts count),
a thin-blow WARN (a strike with no tissue or body mechanics, R80-5, R81-1),
and WARNs on any readout or narrated figure in a fight (R79-6, R81-3); school: blade, japanese, chinese, korean, percussion, boxing, firearms,
kharven (Eastern terms are free and never required). explicit=True adds the floor
guard and the euphemism list (R73-41, R79-7). Run once a turn, fix every FAIL,
read the WARNs without looping on them.

tools.name: codex
tools.description:
Look a term up in The Master Codex, read from the xlsx (R18-6, never from
memory): a glyph token or name, a spell, an alchemical formula, a Pantheon
member, a Wellspring or Family. sheet narrows to one of The Pantheon, Master
Glyph Index, Spell Index, Alchemical Index, Lists. Pack Eighteen step 4a:
query it for anything the scene will work before naming or writing it.

tools.name: codex_check
tools.description:
Pack Eighteen checks 37-39 on a draft against The Master Codex: every
Latinate coinage on the Lists sheet, every [Glyph] token in the Master Glyph
Index, and the Spell Index rows it names (precedent stays a manual call).

tools.name: propose_rule
tools.description:
File a rule Natalie originated at the table as a proposal (pending Isaac's
ratification). Appended to proposals/PROPOSED.md and pushed; folded into the next
amendment pack extraction. rule_text should be the rule as it would read in a pack.

tools.name: ask_chatgpt
tools.description:
Ask ChatGPT (Codex, on Isaac's ChatGPT plan) and get its answer back, in 10 to 90 s.
It works in this repo read-only, with the read-only WOTR tools: give it paths, not
pasted text. Use it for a second opinion, an adversarial review of a draft against the
rules, research that would mean many reads, or a rival take on a beat or a name. Its
answer is input to check, never authority, and it can save nothing.

tools.name: ask_claude
tools.description:
Ask Claude (on Isaac's Claude plan, as Natalie, with this repo's CLAUDE.md) and get its
answer back, in 10 to 120 s: the mirror of ask_chatgpt, so the two check each other.
Read-only: it reads the repo and the read-only WOTR tools and can save nothing. Give it
paths, not pasted text. Its answer is input to check, never authority.

tools.name: research_chatgpt
tools.description:
Hand a real-world research question to ChatGPT (live web search, on Isaac's ChatGPT plan)
and get on with the work: the cited write-up lands in the inbox as a research item in 2 to
10 minutes (read it with inbox). For the science behind an ability, a working, a wound, a
material or a phenomenon: it names the real phenomenon, the governing law with measured
figures, the limits, the failure modes and costs, the nearest fictional precedents, and
every source it opened. Outside research, never a rule source or a verbatim.

tools.name: chatgpt_image
tools.description:
Make one image with ChatGPT's image model (on Isaac's ChatGPT plan), in 30 to 120 s.
It comes back shown inline, saved to ~/wotr-drafts/images/, with a link. Describe the
whole picture: subject, setting, light, palette, medium, framing. WOTR's look is
Arcane and Fullmetal Alchemist, the settings of Bleach and Naruto, Final Fantasy and
Lord of the Mysteries (R53-28, R78-4), vivid and magitech-lit, never Berserk or Vinland. Describe a style rather
than naming a living artist, and no real person's likeness (Isaac's rule: reference,
never copies). The model letters signs and dials on its own, with Earth names
(it wrote "London" on a gauge): ask for no text, or give the exact WOTR words.
OpenAI's model refuses explicit content. name: a short file name.

tools.name: handoff
tools.description:
Leave a research write-up or an image brief for a Claude session; nothing here touches
canon. kind: research | image (R79-12: only these two). body: the write-up with its
sources, or the image brief. One handoff per item; Claude applies or declines each one.

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: What has been handed off (handoff) and not yet applied, oldest first.

tools.name: inbox_done
tools.description:
Close one inbox item after applying or declining it. outcome says which, and what was
written where (e.g. 'applied: ledger_add L-0412' or 'declined: contradicts R71-6').

tools.name: stale_names
tools.description:
The Büri/Moto sweep: every wiki page and scene still carrying a struck
Büri-register term (from the Moto Reversion Ledger's tables: Büri, Ajiin, Altan,
Nüdel, Khar Ild, the Seven Works, Sātūlagi...). scope: all | wiki | scenes.
Returns per-file counts with the governing replacement, worst first. Nothing is
edited; the ruling is Moto in all new prose, old files flagged.

tools.name: scene_brief
tools.description:
The short pre-write for a set piece (R79-2: scene_brief and the full pipeline are
for set pieces only; a turn goes straight to the draft). Give the beat Isaac handed
you; get back the brief to fill before drafting: POV choice (write from whoever knows
least, R5-C1), what the POV knows / wrongly believes / the reader knows, the cost,
the close, each named practitioner's kit; plus FOW lines for the named characters
and the rule loadout for the scene type. The brief lives in the author notes at
archive; nothing of it is printed under the scene. culture is kept for callers and
no longer used.

tools.name: scene_context
tools.description:
The lorebook: paste a draft, a beat, or Isaac's prompt and get back what the wiki
knows about every name in it — character cards (full, capped), pages for places,
artifacts, disciplines and factions (their head), the prior scenes on the same
ground (semantic), struck Büri-register terms, and any name the wiki has no page
for. Call it before drafting and again before posting; nothing is written.
budget caps the reply in characters.

tools.name: cast_index
tools.description:
Who appears in which scene. Matches every wiki character-card name (and the
voice roster) against scenes/, writes scenes/CAST.md and, if missing, a
scenes/ARCS.md reading-order skeleton grouped by the numbered prefixes. Returns
the cast list.

Alias collapsing: short roster names (e.g. 'Aurelian') are collapsed into their
full card name (e.g. 'Aurelian Prudentius Custos Clausorum') when one exists.
Mentions from either form are merged; the heading shows the canonical name with
aliases in parentheses.

tools.name: create_character
tools.description:
Add a new character card: writes the wiki page under the given volume
(Volume I / III / IV / V — Character Cards, or 'Characters'), commits and pushes. markdown is the full card in the seventeen-section
format (see convert_character for the skeleton). Refuses a name that already has a
card; use update_character for those. Numbers must come from the FOW tables or
Isaac; anything estimated is marked pending in the card.

tools.name: update_character
tools.description:
Replace an existing character card's body in the wiki (same id, links
survive), then commit and push. markdown is the full
replacement card, not a diff.

tools.name: trello_cards
tools.description:
List the cards in a Trello board export (Trello → Menu → Print and export →
Export as JSON). Filter by list name or a keyword. Use the card name with
convert_character(source=<the card's text>) or pass the whole export path.

tools.name: convert_character
tools.description:
Convert an old character record (a Trello card's JSON or text, an old sheet,
any prose) into the current system: returns a conversion brief — the source
material, every old-register name flagged with its Moto-canon form, the
seventeen-section skeleton with what each section must hold and which rules
govern it, the FOW Band / Stage / Tier Grade tables so numbers land on the
real scale, and the rule loadout. You write the card from the brief, then
create_character saves it. Never invent a number: anything the source does not
give and the tables do not fix is written as 'pending Isaac' in the card.
source may be raw text, a JSON string, or a card name when json_path is given.

tools.name: fronts
tools.description:
The Fronts as clocks: want, last move, position, the next tick and the pace in story days (R72-20).
Filter by thread ('Kharven', 'Korvaeth', 'Mu-jin'); clocks are never printed in play (R72-21).

tools.name: advance_front
tools.description:
Tick a Front's clock by one by hand, for a move his acts caused or sped, with the next tick if known.
The calendar ticks come from pass_time (R72-20); the Front resolves when its clock fills.

tools.name: set_front_clock
tools.description:
Rewrite a Front's clock (4 to 6 consequences, the last how it resolves or breaks) and/or its pace in story days per tick.
His acts can speed, slow or stop a Front (R72-20): pace_days=0 stops the calendar ticking it.

tools.name: add_front
tools.description: Open a new Front: name, thread, what it wants, its clock (4 to 6 consequences) and its pace in story days per tick (R72-20).

tools.name: pass_time
tools.description:
Story time passes on a thread: every open Front there with a pace banks the days and ticks offscreen once per pace spent (R72-20).
story_date (Y-M-D in the Accord count, month 1 to 13, day 1 to 28) sets the thread's date, and given alone passes the days since the last one.

tools.name: due
tools.description:
What has come due: Ledger lines whose story date has come (today, Y-M-D, or the thread's held date), whose trigger was marked fired, or whose clock is full (R72-22).
A line with neither (every row from before R72) keeps the old reading by sessions_old, marked 'no date or trigger yet'; the bill arrives as an offer with terms (R72-23).

tools.name: ledger_add
tools.description:
Enter a Ledger line with its thread and a due_date (story date, Y-M-D) or a named due_trigger (R72-22); due_condition is the old name for a trigger.
Categories: the dead, injuries and reserve, debts, who knows what, renown (per audience: public, army, sects, guilds; 'reputation' still accepted), canon conflicts, bonds, heat (one per thread, level in words), projects (ticks 4 to 8), roads (ticks 4 to 6).

tools.name: ledger_mark
tools.description:
Mark a standing Ledger line: what fed or strained a bond (R72-24), heat raised or cooled to a level in words, or ticks filled on a project or road clock (R72-28, R72-29).
A full clock comes due through due(); how says what moved it.

tools.name: fire_trigger
tools.description:
Mark a named trigger fired (words from it, or a line id): every open Ledger line waiting on it comes due (R72-22).
Silent upkeep does this through session_end's fired list; call this when it fires mid-session.

tools.name: ledger_collect
tools.description: Mark a Ledger line collected: what happened when it came due.

tools.name: roster
tools.description:
The NPC roster for a thread: want, refusal, what they know, the live lie and its tell, doing now and where they stand with him (R72-25, R72-26).
public=True prints only name, look, voice and role, the face a player may see (R72-40).

tools.name: npc_set
tools.description: Create or update an NPC on the roster; only the fields you pass change. lie and tell are a lie the NPC's want makes them tell and how it shows, only where they would lie (R72-25 as amended by R79-2); doing_now and stands_with (owed, slighted, warm, afraid, or words) are kept current by silent upkeep as scenes happen, never printed; look and role are the public face.

tools.name: scene_menu
tools.description:
Seeds for the Scene Menu, offered only when Isaac opens without a beat: three OOC hooks from anywhere, with no source rule and no reward or penalty lines (R79-2, amending R72-17). The Front, the Ledger and a barely seen character below are suggestions, not slots.
He picks in a word and the turn opens on that hook in the world. There is no Rumor Mill (R79-2).

tools.name: session_end
tools.description:
Silent upkeep at a scene's end, then the archive (R79-8): nothing printed beyond a
one-line confirmation. days or story_date pass story time as pass_time does; fired marks
triggers; ledger takes ledger_add fields for lines that bind; fronts takes front_id,
what_happened and next_move; npcs takes npc_set fields (doing_now, stands_with) for the
NPCs the scene moved; cards takes {name, markdown} with the full replacement card
(update_character) for lasting changes only: a wound that stays, Crystal State, Level,
Stage, a technique he approved, renown. title (with scene_markdown) archives the scene
as archive_scene does. Each write is an agent ruling logged with the session.

tools.name: reconcile
tools.description:
Mechanical consistency checks across the wiki, the scenes and the index:
duplicate pages, a character's Stage or Level stated differently in a scene than
on the card, a Wellspring named with the wrong Family.

tools.name: pack_impact
tools.description:
Before a new amendment pack is extracted: which live rules share distinctive
vocabulary with its text, so collisions are read before they become conflicts.

tools.name: timeline
tools.description:
scenes/TIMELINE.md: every scene in reading order with the in-world moment the
text states. Created as a skeleton on first call; edit the 'placed' column.

tools.name: gap_fill
tools.description:
Advisory only (R79-12): Pack Thirteen §5's eight-step gap-fill pass, for a set piece
or a fight Isaac submits, never a gate on a turn. Structured report: beat inventory,
logic audit, stratum audit, physics audit, body audit, phenomenon audit, vocabulary
pass, prose pass. Counts what can be counted and asks the question each step exists
to ask; nothing in it is a FAIL.

tools.name: scene_text
tools.description:
The scene's narration text in the cast-file format: a `# Title` line, paragraphs separated by
blank lines, `---` for section breaks, author notes and markdown removed. This is exactly what the
narrator reads. To give characters their own voices, insert speaker tags where the voice changes —
[Verinus] before a spoken line, [narrator] to return — and let the prose set the delivery: a dialogue
tag or the narration around a line ("he said quietly", "roared", "after a silence", "she laughed and
said") becomes delivery after a colon ([Verinus: quiet], [Gimbzo: loud], [Ruin: beat]; words: slow,
slower, fast, faster, quiet, loud, whisper, beat, long beat) or a performed cue inside the line ([laugh],
[chuckle], [sigh], [gasp], [cough], [clear throat]) — only where the text says so, never invented.
Italic direct thought is the POV character's own voice. Change nothing else, and pass the result to
cast_scene. Untagged text is the narrator's.

tools.name: cast_scene
tools.description:
Save a speaker-tagged script for a scene (scenes/cast/<scene>.cast.md) so narrate_scene renders
each character in their own voice. `script` is the text from scene_text with [Name] tags inserted
(see scene_text). The tagged text with its tags removed must match the scene word for word — the
tool refuses anything that drops or changes words and says where. Speakers with no entry in
build/voices.yaml get a stable pool voice; the reply lists them so Isaac can assign voices.

tools.name: narrate_scene
tools.description:
Render one scene of the archive to an MP3, in the background on Isaac's PC (build/audio_export.py).
`engine`: "local" (Kokoro/Chatterbox/Qwen, free) or "elevenlabs" (every speaker through the
_elevenlabs map in build/voices.yaml; costs characters on Isaac's ElevenLabs plan, so ask him which
he wants before choosing it — the reply states the character count). ElevenLabs renders are
named *-eleven and sit beside the local ones. `scene` is a scene file name or title (or a unique part of one). If the
scene has a cast file (cast_scene), every tagged speaker gets their own voice from build/voices.yaml
and `voice` sets only the narrator; otherwise `voice` reads the whole scene — a built-in Kokoro voice,
a voices.yaml name, a custom style file in build/voices/, or a blend like "af_heart:0.6,bm_george:0.4".
Returns the job id, a time estimate and where the file will be; narration_status gives the link.

tools.name: narration_status
tools.description:
Narration jobs started with narrate_scene (running / done / failed) and every rendered scene
with the link to play it: over the public connector a URL on this server; on the desktop the file path.
Audio also lands in the Google Drive folder War of the Realms — Documents/Arcs/Audio when Drive is mounted.

tools.name: lookup
tools.description:
One page or word list from an outside reference, for ideas: never canon, never a rule source, never a
verbatim field. WOTR canon governs every fact and number; borrowed moves get WOTR's own mechanism and name.
Wikis (query = a page title or search words; the exact title wins):
  superpower (powers: capabilities, applications, limitations), vsbattles (character kits: abilities,
  named techniques, weaknesses), powerscaling, hxh (Nen, conditions and vows), jjk (cursed techniques,
  Domains, binding vows), bleach (releases), naruto (jutsu, combos), dragonball, onepiece, fma (alchemy),
  finalfantasy, arcane (magitech), lotm (Pathways, a Stage-like ladder), reverend-insanity (costed
  cultivation), worm (power classes and their strange limits), wiktenauer (historical fencing:
  guards, measure, plays), tolkien (the land), wikipedia (physics, anatomy, history), wiktionary
  (definitions, etymology, archaic words), wikisource (public-domain texts: sagas, manuals, period prose).
Words: datamuse (a bare query finds words meaning like it; Datamuse parameters pass through:
  rel_jjb=blood adjectives for a noun, rel_jja=sword nouns for an adjective, sl=krang sounds like,
  rel_rhy=steel rhymes, rel_trg=forge associated words, ml=bright&topics=metal), jisho (Japanese words
  with readings and senses, for Moto names and manga sound words).
Spells: dnd5e (an SRD spell by name, for school-of-magic brainstorms).

tools.name: research
tools.description:
Outside research on the open web through Agent Reach (search and page reading on Isaac's machine;
    a page it cannot read is opened in a headless browser instead).
    For real-world facts before writing: physics, anatomy and wounds, history, arms and armor, materials,
    trades. Searches the question, reads the top `read` result pages (0 for snippets only) and every page
    in `urls`, and when `power` is given pulls that power's Superpower Wiki page (lookup reads the other
reference wikis and word lists). Returns the sources' own
    text with their URLs for you to read and cite: outside research, never canon and never a rule source;
    it does not go in a verbatim field. A failed source is named, not retried.

tools.name: skill
tools.description:
The WOTR skills (wotr-write, wotr-rp, wotr-npc, wotr-name, wotr-technique, wotr-start, ...), so no one
has to add them to their account. name="" lists them with when to use each; skill(name) returns the
skill to follow; file="references/x.md" returns one of its reference files.

skill_note: (Served by the WOTR MCP. Where this names a repo path, a shell command or Claude Code, use the matching WOTR MCP tool; a file under references/ loads with skill(name, file).)
